items.title: GTA 6 Launch Causes Massive Spike in Traffic for Internet Provider Xfinity
items.excerpt: Internet provider Xfinity has reported a massive spike in traffic on Xbox consoles for GTA 6's New Zealand launch.
items.content_text: Internet provider Xfinity has reported a massive spike in traffic on Xbox consoles for GTA 6's New Zealand launch. Xfinity says it saw a jump in Xbox hardware traffic four times more than normal around the time GTA 6 became available in New Zealand. Although Xfinity provides its services in the United States, Xbox users were able to take advantage of a loophole that let them change their console's region to New Zealand, allowing them start playing the game early despite their actual geographic location. It's one of the only real notable advantages Xbox has had over PlayStation with this game, as Rockstar secured a marketing deal to advertise GTA 6 as playing best on PS5. However, these hours of early access have proven to be very lucrative for Xbox players. As a result, tons of footage for the game has been circulating on social media all day long. Major content creators also took advantage of the New Zealand trick, resulting in record-breaking viewership across platforms like Twitch . As of this afternoon, Twitch reported that tens of millions of watch hours had already been accumulated. Right now, we still don't know how many copies of GTA 6 have sold, but we'll likely hear something by the end of this week or very early next week, depending on how quickly Rockstar wants to boast. This is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all-time, after all, and the official numbers will likely be eyewatering. From a critical perspective, GTA 6 has received nothing but praise. IGN gave the game a 10 for its impeccable attention to detail and unprecedented depth, but we weren't alone in that analysis. The game is currently tied with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the highest rated game on Metacritic. It's also nominated for Game of the Year , in addition to seven other awards at The Game Awards.

items.title: GTA 6 Doesn't Let Players Pick Up Prostitutes, but Rockstar Has a Logical Reason for It
items.excerpt: Rockstar Games has revealed why they chose to forego the ability to pick up prostitutes in GTA 6.
items.content_text: Rockstar Games has revealed why they chose to forego the ability to pick up prostitutes in GTA 6 . That's right — GTA 6 doesn't let you pick up ladies of the night when you're feeling lonely anymore. No, the reason isn't because the game has "gone woke" or anything like that; instead, it's for narrative purposes. As you may already know, Rockstar has put the focus of GTA 6 on a couple. The entire story largely hinges on the romantic pair at the very least having an interest of pursuing a relationship with each other, if not being madly in love, should the player take them down that road. As a result, it wouldn't make much sense to have them out there cheating on each other in dark alleys. Although Michael was a married man in GTA 5, he was not happily married, and spent most of the story dealing with the fact that his own wife cheated on him. Rockstar issued a statement to Shacknews about its decision to remove some features that were in previous GTA games, such as the ability to pick up prostitutes. “GTA 6 is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run," reads Rockstar's statement. "While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in 6 has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon - things like wanted system, the radio, robberies and car theft. Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTA 6, but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia's story.” Players have been able to pick up prostitutes since GTA 3. It has been a controversial staple of the franchise, and often an example of the morally bankrupt deeds the sandbox crime-simulator allows for. Mainstream news outlets had a field day with the fact that you could pick up a gal, pay them for sex, and even kill them to get your money back. That, however, won't be possible in GTA 6. With that said, there are strippers in GTA 6, and you can even visit the club together as a couple. However, it's one thing to watch someone dance naked on a stage and another to get down and dirty with them, so it's easy to see why Rockstar would pull back in one area versus another. IGN was pretty blown away by GTA 6 and gave it a 10, noting that the game is masterfully crafted and filled with an unprecdented amount of depth and detail: "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played," reads an excerpt from our review.
items.title_en: GTA 6 Doesn't Let Players Pick Up Prostitutes, but Rockstar Has a Logical Reason for It

items.title: 43 Army Members Reenlisted in Exchange for Paid Time Off to Play GTA 6
items.excerpt: If you’ve been following the GTA 6 hype train, you’ll probably remember the time that an army battalion went viral for offering service members four days of paid time off to play Rockstar's highly-anticipated game if they reenlisted.
items.content_text: If you’ve been following the GTA 6 hype train, you’ll probably remember the time that an army battalion went viral for offering service members four days of paid time off to play Rockstar's highly-anticipated game if they reenlisted. The news became a hot topic after a flyer advertising the paid leave was first shared online back in August. Now that GTA 6 is almost upon us (or, in some regions, already out ), we’ve finally gotten an update on how many soldiers actually took up the battalion's offer. The flyer, dated July 28, concerned the 9th Engineer Battalion in Fort Stewart, Georgia, and promised a “special reenlistment incentive” by giving eligible service members four days off to play the game from November 20 - 23, 2026. This was done specifically to “coincide with the highly anticipated release of the video game Grand Theft Auto VI,” with the goal of “promoting retention, boosting morale, and rewarding the continued dedication of the Soldiers within the 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion.” Three months later, military-focused news outlet Task and Purpose has shared a follow-up on this incentive, confirming that 43 members of the battalion took up the offer. Two of these soldiers spoke with the platform — one being combat engineer Sgt. Jamire Smith, who says he signed up for the GTA 6-specific PTO and an additional six more years in the armed forces. However, this extra time came with a nice $60,000 bonus, owed to his special training learning how to drive heavy breaching vehicles. “I’m all campaign. I’m all about the heist. I think I have a good 24 hours to waste on it,” he told the outlet. “I was actually in the process of getting out, I was towards my final stages of getting out … but my company and the battalion helped me navigate through that and they showed me that there’s still a need for me, and that I am still a clear and value asset to the team, and so that’s really what drove me to say ‘let’s keep going, let’s keep driving.’ Maybe be a lifer in this, since I already made it my career.” Task and Purpose even got in touch with the person responsible for coming up with the campaign, Staff Sgt. Brittany Wolfer, a career counselor who explained why she chose to use the game as an eye-catching way to get soldiers to stay in the service. “I brought it to my battalion commander and he’s a little bit older, but he did play GTA 2 at some point, so he was like, ‘Yeah I’m down for it,’” Wolfer explained. “I came into [the unit], there hadn’t been a counselor for about eight months, so there [were] a lot of gaps and things that were falling through, because the soldiers didn’t have that presence within the formation. This was just a way to grab people’s attention and kind of be like, ‘Hey, here I am. I’m the person you’re gonna come talk to,’ and [it] kind of snowballed from there.” Wolfer made it clear that she knows the GTA 6-focused PTO dates won’t be a “deciding factor” in someone’s decision to reenlist, but said the idea was a way to “bridge that gap” between soldiers and their senior command “to where that lower soldier still knows that their battalion commander or their senior leadership cares about them and sees what they’re interested in. And that’s kind of what this was for.” GTA 6 releases for players in the United States at 12am ET / 9pm PT. Despite not even being officially out yet, it has already scored eight nominations at the 2026 Game Awards , and is one of the highest-rated games in Metacritic history . You can check out our review for the game right here on IGN, which we scored a glowing 10 out of 10.

items.title: Alienware's 39" 5K Monitor With RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Technology Hits a New Price Low for Black Friday
items.excerpt: A monitor that excels at both gaming and workstation productivity.
items.content_text: Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology." You can finally get your hands on one. The new Alienware AW3926QW has just been listed at Dell for $1,099.99 with free delivery. For Black Friday, Best Buy is offering it for $100 less . This monitor excels at both gaming and workstation use thanks to its unparalleled text clarity. It also comes with a 3 year warranty that covers OLED burn-in. Save $100 Off the Alienware 39" 5K OLED Gaming Monitor The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive technology is the RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in. The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike. Tandem and RGB stripe technologies aside, the AW3926QW is also Alienware's first 5K OLED monitor. With an impressive 5120 x 2160 resolution, this 39" monitor boasts a pixel density of 143ppi. That's even sharper than an already impressive 32" 4K monitor, with its pixel density of 138ppi. A 39" monitor is pretty wide, so the AW3926QW employs a 1500R curve to balance it out. 1500R is pretty moderate as far as curved monitors go, so although you'll be able to see the entire monitor within your field of view, it won't significantly distort peripheral images. OLED monitors are known for their extreme fast response time and perfect black levels, making them ideal for gaming. The AW3926QW ups the ante with its 165Hz refresh rate at 4K and support for AMD FreeSync Premium Pro and NVIDIA G-Sync compatibility. It has both DisplayPort 2.1 and HDMI 2.1 ports so you'll be able to connect it to just about any modern day graphics card without the need for adapters. Alienware also backs the monitor up with a 3 year warranty that covers OLED burn-in. items.title: A GTA 6 Location Was Teased by Rockstar All the Way Back in 2021 — And What's Inside Was Worth the Wait
items.excerpt: In 2021, Rockstar fans believed that a GTA 6 screenshot was snuck into the GTA trilogy collection, but there's more to this theory than meets the eye.
items.content_text: SPOILER WARNING: This article features details on a GTA 6 Easter egg. Although it won't ruin the game's story or anything like that, we recognize some people want to organically discover and find interesting things on their own. You've been warned! In 2021, Rockstar Games released the somewhat controversial remastered collection of the PS2 era GTA titles. It was... a mess, to say the least. However, one notable thing came from that collection, but fans weren't sure if it actually meant anything. There was a picture of a house in this new version of GTA: San Andreas that wasn't there in the original game, and it didn't look like a location from any other GTA game. Fans theorized this was actually our first look at GTA 6 ... and it turns out, they were right! The house is real. It's located in Leonard County, in the suburb of Belville (shoutout Jared from the GTA mapping community for discovering this). However, that's just the tip of the iceberg. If you approach the house's garage, you can actually break in. Upon entry, it becomes clear this is a lair for some kind of conspiracy theorist. These aren't just ordinary in-universe ramblings — they're from someone who believes they are in a video game. All credit goes to Jared from the GTA VI Mapping server. The house is located in Belville. (https://t.co/hWt1Koz3uz) https://t.co/t2ZsSRPQFI — GTA Wiki (@GTAWikiOfficial) November 18, 2026 Various notes and writings on the wall point out that they can't leave Lenoida at all. They tried to purchase a ticket to Los Santos and couldn't, nor could they drive out of the state, and instead are planning to get a boat to try and escape. They also noted that there are an extraordinary amount of doppelgangers in reference to NPCs, that there is nothing behind closed doors, their own neighbors can't enter their homes, and that people phase through walls or "glitch." There's also a graph that shows a comically large spike in violent crime and a bunch of 6s written all over the place, likely poking fun at some of the people who drove themselves mad theorizing about this very game. Perhaps one of the most notable bits is that this conspiracy theorist has determined two people, who go by "J" (Jason) and "L" (Lucia), are immune to whatever problems they are experiencing, suggesting they have freedom and autonomy. Ironically, they may have the least amount of autonomy, though, since they are controlled by the player, but they respawn, are largely free of longterm legal consequences, and can cause tons of mayhem, so they're less restricted than NPCs. It's a very silly Easter egg, and one that leans into the absurdity of the GTA community in many ways. It's unclear whether this house was always meant to be like this, or if someone at the studio decided to have some fun with it after they saw how mad it drove fans. Either way, it gave me a good chuckle. In related news, GTA 6 is already shattering all kinds of records despite not being out globally. The game is driving tons of traffic to Twitch, YouTube, and Kick, with millions of people just watching the game. As for its critical reception, GTA 6 got a 10/10 from IGN and its critical praise has been echoed across the industry. In addition to being nominated for Game of the Year , GTA 6 is currently tied with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest rated game of all-time on Metacritic . While its position could change as more reviews trickle in over the next few weeks, it's clear this game is a gargantuan hit (though that likely isn't surprising).

items.title: Burger King’s Chocolate Whopper Prank Is Being Turned Into a Real Burger
items.content_text: In 2018, Burger King posted a Chocolate Whopper as an April Fool’s Joke. Nearly a decade later, the decadent burger is actually coming to life. The Chocolate Whopper is coming to Burger King Korea’s new flagship restaurant, the Flameground, which recently launched its first location in Seoul. Flameground somehow turns Burger King food into a luxurious dining experience, showcasing the fast-food chain’s most experimental creations. Burger King Korea accounts have shared AI-generated renderings of the Chocolate Whopper’s concept: layers of sauces and brownie patties encased in a chocolate fudge bun. We'll have to wait until the burger launches on November 19 to see what it actually looks and tastes like. Unfortunately, the Chocolate Whopper is getting an extremely limited rollout. The burger isn’t even coming to general Burger King Korea locations, and is instead entirely restricted to the single Flameground restaurant, which requires a reservation. The generated rendering is jam-packed, to say the least. Each burger is handmade, and orders are restricted to one per person with daily quantity limits. The Chocolate Whopper will also only be available as a dine-in experience, no take-out allowed, so Burger King is really trying to stop you from sharing. Ahead of the launch, Burger King also reshared the original April Fool's prank video. The original prank featured some candied tomatoes the real version understandably skips out on. Burger King Korea launched its first Flameground restaurant this past September. The Seongsu location currently offers three signature burgers: the K-Cube Galbi, the Philly Cheese Steak, and the Memphis BBQ. These are priced between ₩12,900 and ₩13,900, equivalent to around $10 USD. The restaurant has yet to announce pricing for the Chocolate Whopper. The entire Burger King franchise has taken to wacky marketing, though most of the chain’s big promotions stick to licensed collaborations. For example, Burger King Italy just launched a Magic: The Gathering meal with an exclusive deck box everyone has been trying to get their hands on. Surprisingly, the fast-food chain has yet to announce any new food items inspired by GTA 6 , which features the parody restaurant Burger Shot.

items.title: New Avengers: Doomsday Posters Reveal Key Characters and Tease Thor’s Odinforce
items.excerpt: Marvel has revealed a massive lineup of new posters for Avengers: Doomsday, teasing major characters and a potentially huge upgrade for Thor.
items.content_text: Apparently, no one told Marvel that GTA VI is out today, because they've been busy showing off new glimpses of Avengers: Doomsday. In addition to a behind-the-scenes video featuring Robert Downey, Jr. , Marvel has also revealed a massive lineup of posters showcasing the film's ensemble cast. These 11 posters form one large montage showing the combined forces of the X-Men, Fantastic Four, and Avengers in battle against Downey's Doctor Doom and his army of Sentinels and Doombots. Get a closer look at all these connecting posters in the slideshow gallery below: These images tease some interesting new details for the film, like giving us a better look at Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler in costume and showcasing the Doombots (Doctor Doom's android servants/bodyguards) for the first time. Perhaps most interesting is the poster featuring Chris Hemsworth's Thor and Chris Evans' Steve Rogers. Steve is wielding Mjolnir and channeling the weapon's signature blue lightning, but Thor's Stormbreaker is instead summoning yellow lightning. This has already led fans to speculate that Thor is now empowered by the Odinforce, signalling a major power upgrade for this already mighty Avenger. Though if the Doomsday trailers are any indication, that's not going to be enough to stop Doom. We also have to wonder if the character pairings in these posters are significant and meant to tease various team-ups in the film. Certainly, Steve and Thor have a long history together. And we doubt it was merely coincidence that Marvel chose to pair Vanessa Kirby's Invisible Woman and Tenoch Huerta's Namor, given the (mostly one-sided) romantic attachment they share in the comics. But what about the rest of the posters? Will Channing Tatum's Gambit partner up with Florence Pugh's Yelena Belova? What about Tom Hiddleston's Loki and Rebecca Romijn's Mystique? We'll have to wait until Doomsday hits theaters on December 18 to find out. In the meantime, Marvel has already begun teasing Doomsday's sequel, 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars, revealing that the film will be very different in terms of tone and genre . We've also learned that R yan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman have been given writing credits on Doomsday , suggesting that Deadpool and Wolverine will appear in the film. items.title: The Wachowskis Move to Reclaim The Matrix Rights From Skydance
items.excerpt: The future of The Matrix franchise is suddenly in doubt, as Lilly and Lana Wachowski move to reclaim the copyright to the iconic sci-fi franchise from Warner Bros.
items.content_text: The future of The Matrix franchise is looking increasingly murky. According to The Puck Report , Lana and Lilly Wachowski have formally notified Warner Bros. of their move to reclaim the copyright to the iconic sci-fi franchise. If successful, the Wachowskis would regain the rights to the series on the 30th anniversary of the original film's release in 2029. This move comes as the studio is developing a fifth The Matrix movie , with Drew Goddard attached to write and direct and Lana Wachowski herself executive producing. That project may give the Wachowskis extra leverage in their negotiations with Warners. Will this derail development on The Matrix 5? Not necessarily. The site also notes that WB's new parent company Skydance seems confident in its ability to negotiate a new deal, building on previous successes renegotiating the copyright for The Godfather and acquiring The Terminator rights in 2011. The Puck Report also alludes to a potential legal hurdle on the Wachowskis' side, as it could be argued that the original The Matrix screenplay was part of a work-for-hire arrangement with Warner Bros. back in the '90s. All of this may suggest that the more likely outcome is that the Wachowskis negotiate a new, more lucrative deal and Skydance retains the rights to The Matrix for the foreseeable future. Despite Lilly Wachowski publicly distancing herself from the property , The Puck Report writes, "From what I hear, the sisters have been encouraging of the newest sequel and have even increased their involvement lately." Little is currently known about The Matrix 5 beyond Goddard's involvement. There's currently no release date, nor is it clear whether series stars Keanu Reeves and Carrie-Anne Moss will return or if the focus will shift to a new cast of cyberpunk martial artists. But the studio seems to have high hopes for the sequel, despite its predecessor, 2021's The Matrix Resurrections, proving to be a box office dud. It certainly didn't help that the film debuted during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic and premiered on HBO Max the same day as it did in theaters, prompting a lawsuit from Village Roadshow . items.title: GTA 6 Shatters Streaming Records Before It Even Launches Globally
items.excerpt: GTA 6 is already breaking records, despite not having even been out for a full day yet.
items.content_text: GTA 6 is already breaking records, despite not having even been out for a full day yet. According to StreamCharts, GTA 6 shattered livestreaming viewership records following its release in New Zealand. Streamers began grinding the game at the earliest hours of the morning here in the United States thanks to handy loopholes on Xbox, allowing them to get a head start on things. As of 12:30 UTC today, the game crossed 6.38 million concurrent viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick. This is nearly four times the previous record holder, which was Valorant's closed beta. Twitch also provided first details about the game's performance using its own internal data to IGN. GTA 6 smashed the Valorant on Twitch record, which stood at 1.7 million concurrent viewers in 2020. On Twitch, GTA 6 is at tens of millions of hours watched, just a couple hours in. The equivalent of more than 1,500 years of nonstop viewing. Top GTA Streamer Rubius reached 311k live viewers for GTAVI within an hour of starting his broadcast. GTA 6 in North America is technically not available to play yet but the streamer has already seen: Twitch viewership is up 111% compared with this time last week. At one point early this morning Twitch had more than 3.3 million live viewers in the GTA 6 category. Twitch recently revealed to IGN that GTA 5 has accumulated 9 billion hours watched over the course of its entire lifetime, making it an absolute juggernaut for the platform. It's one of the most-watched games and it's likely that GTA 6 will retain get at least one or two more big boosts in viewership. The game is rumored to come to PC early next year and its online mode is also expected sometime in 2027, both of which will likely be events in their own rights. IGN recently spoke with a number of content creators about how they're planning to handle GTA 6 and how long they think this game will remain relevant. Although some streamers believe this game will only be lucrative for a couple of weeks, others think there's potential for it to be mined for months and years to come. IGN gave the game a 10/10 , noting that the game is simply unmatched in its depth, quality, and detail. The game is currently the highest-rated game in history on Metacritic with an unprecedented 99 average score. "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played," reads an excerpt from our review. items.title: I've Played the First 30 Minutes of GTA 6 on Every Console, Here's How Performance Compares
items.excerpt: How GTA 6 performance compares across every console, based on our early tests.
items.content_text: GTA 6 came out in certain parts of the world this morning, and I've taken the opportunity to dive in and see how the game holds up on all four of the current-generation consoles. Over the last few hours I've played through the first 30 minutes or so on the Xbox Series S , Xbox Series X, PlayStation 5 and the PlayStation 5 Pro, and largely, the game runs fine no matter which version you're playing. But, that doesn't mean there aren't differences between each of them. The elephant in the room with all of the machines is the frame rate. That's not surprising, Rockstar came out and told us that the game would be "targeting" 30 fps on all the consoles . But what was surprising is how different that 30 fps feels depending on what you're playing it on. The biggest example of this is obviously the Xbox Series S. Throughout the prologue and the first part of the first chapter, GTA 6 sits at a pretty steady 30fps, but there are occasionally dips as low as 24fps. Even outside of those super-low dips, turning the camera can sometimes cause the frame rate to jitter a little bit, and while the fps only drops to 27 or 28 in these scenarios, it results in movement that feels like it's dragging on something. On the base PS5 and Xbox Series X, however, the frame rate stays pretty much locked at 30fps, with only occasional dips to the 27-29 fps range. Keep in mind, though, that I've only got through the first mission, and there is going to be some chaos later in the game that's likely going to wreak more havoc on the 6-year-old CPU in any of the consoles. I know that Digital Foundry has already found a couple of instances on the base PS5, for example. I just don't have the explosives to make that happen yet. The PS5 Pro is, unsurprisingly, the best way to play GTA 6, and at least in my time with the game so far, it's the version of the game I'd recommend for most people who have the budget to support it. Rockstar's implementation of PSSR really cleans up the presentation, and the ray traced shadows are a godsend in some of the darker scenes I've seen so far. It's also the smoothest version of the game, and I didn't see any dips like I have on all of the other consoles. It's worth keeping in mind, though, that if you want to buy a PS5 Pro right now, you're basically stuck paying more than $1,400 for the privilege. I don't know if it's worth paying that much, when you can literally save half of that purchasing cost, and the only thing you're really losing out on is better shadows and a couple of frame drops. Even if you only have the cash for the Xbox Series S, the game still plays fine . You'll get more frame dips, and you'll have to deal with more aliasing on hard edges. The FSR 4.1 implementation is doing a lot of work here , and it looks great considering that it's rendering at 720p and getting upscaled up to 1080p. It's probably not the way that I will play the game over the coming weeks, but if that's what you have, GTA 6 is still an awesome game so far. Now, I have about an hour played total on both my Xbox and PlayStation accounts, and obviously a lot can change over the course of this very long game. I'm going to keep at it, and hopefully GTA 6 continues to be a showcase of what these consoles are capable of at this point in their lifespan. And, at least at this point, I have no reason to suspect that it won't. items.content_text: Audiences will learn to love AI-generated games, the former CEO of GTA publisher Take-Two Interactive has said — as soon as they churn out a 'Toy Story moment' of quality. Speaking to The Game Business , ex-Take-Two exec Ben Feder claimed that gamers who are sceptical about AI-made slop would be won over when a great example eventually comes along, with any resistance then melting away. Feder served at the company behind releases such as BioShock and Borderlands from 2007 to 2011, before subsequently joining Tencent Games, and serving on the boards of numerous other companies such as Bad Robot and Epic Games. The comparison with Toy Story here is Feder equating the rise of generative AI (replacing games designed and coded by humans) to the emergence of computer animation in the world of animated movies (largely replacing hand-drawn techniques). "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business . "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar launched Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it. "My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West," Feder continued. "In the East, they've already accepted it." It's easy to see what Feder is implying, although the similarities between the two situations don't feel clear cut. Yes, Disney fans (and employees) were divided on the art of hand-drawn animation being superseded by an all-digital alternative. But the latter still requires considerable human skill to create — even if an artist is now using a stylus on an iPad rather than drawing with ink on paper. Comparing this to the vibe-coded future of game development now rapidly bearing down upon us, generated by a few quick prompts and powered by GPU-hogging and potentially copyright-infringing AI tools, and it all seems something quite different. Perhaps unsurprisingly, Feder is now a managing partner at Tirta Ventures, a venture capital firm that is keen to invest in AI-generated games. "Our gaming backgroundhelps us identify AI-native platforms shaping how people play, create, and transact in digital environments," Tirta's website states. The timing of Feder's statement — and his background at Take-Two — is also somewhat ironic, in the wake of Rockstar releasing the masterpiece that is GTA 6 after a decade of development, creating perhaps the biggest monument to game development without the widespread use of AI tools we're ever likely to see. That's what the former boss of Take-Two thinks about AI, but what does the current boss of Take-Two think about the tech? Last month, Strauss Zelnick said AI is a valuable tool, but insisted humans will remain at the ehart of what the company does. “One of our division heads has said to his team, ‘You’re not gonna be replaced by AI, but if you’re not careful you’ll be replaced by someone who knows how to use AI,’” Zelnick said . “I’m fond of saying AI is a collection of datasets, compute, and large language models. That’s what it is. And datasets, by definition, are backward looking. That’s all they are. And creativity, at its best, is forward looking. [...]" If you're keen to play the (human-created) GTA 6 this week, IGN has you covered — including the GTA 6 global release times , as well as details on the last-minute PS5 update you'll need to download . In case you missed it, last night we learned the real-life identity of GTA 6's Lucia . And we're now live with our GTA 6 launch blog , which we'll use to fill you in on everything else about the game over the coming hours.

items.title: Import AI 481: AI sub-contractors; a wet lab for AI; and subterfuge during development
items.content_text: Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. If you’d like to support this, please subscribe. Subscribe now AI systems are getting good at sub-contracting to make themselves better: …AI can now productively spend money to improve itself… Researchers have developed FrontierML, a benchmark “that measures how well agents turn capital into model performance on challenging, end-to-end machine learning tasks.” It shows that today’s frontier systems are already able to, when given some money, turn this into improving their own performance on a basket of 21 distinct tasks. 21 long-horizon tasks “inspired by real work at frontier labs, neolabs, and academic institutions”. These tasks span six category areas, including LLM training, efficiency, vision & audio, computer use, applied NLP, and math & games. “Each task provides the agent with the same setup: a 12-hour CPU sandbox, a wallet with $10, $50, or $200, a few validation samples, and a task description.” Example task: Agents try to solve the tasks in pretty different ways. E.g, for one task about generating screenshots, the top-scoring agent fine-tuned a diffusion model using LoRA, while other high-scoring approaches involved an LLM writing a drawing program that is then rendered. Key features: Scaling spending : “Give agents $10, $50, and $200 per task to spend on training compute and data, and evaluate whether agents can use the additional capital productively,” they write. “In our experiments, we find that stronger agents are able to reliably improve their submissions with greater access to capital.” Open-ended & end-to-end : “In each task, agents can choose architectures, source data, implement training, provision compute, evaluate checkpoints, and optimize inference,” they write. One notable observation is that agents do quite a lot of novel stuff; “in 28% of trajectories, agents add newly trained parts to pretrained models or train a new model from scratch.” Decent verification: “Agents submit an inference server that serves their model on an air-gapped H100 machine,” they write. “To disincentivize overfitting, we provide limited validation samples and evaluate on a large out-of-distribution held-out test set, not shown to the agent”. Results : The authors measure performance by looking at the change in mean score over the 21 tasks when given additional money. Their baseline is a human researcher, which is able to get a 56 point boost when given $10 and a 66.1 boost when given $200. By comparison, the best performing system, Opus 5.5, gets a 45.4 boost with $10, and a 58.8 boost with $200. The highest ranking open weight model is Kimi K3.1 Pro which gets 25.5 with $10 and 29.6 with $200. Why this matters - AI systems are not only going to be able to build themselves, but they can creatively sub-contract: When trying to solve complex problems, people don’t work alone. In fact, they often try to farm out bits of work to specialists around them to help make themselves more effective. FrontierML shows that today’s powerful AI systems are getting increasingly adept at doing this for ML research. This both highlights the advancing capabilities of these systems for AI R&D and also points towards a future machine economy where AI systems sub-contract out different bits of work to other systems. Read more: FrontierML: a challenging, end-to-end machine learning benchmark (FrontierML) . *** Symptoms of the singularity: a wet lab built for AI: …Petrichor is a startup that gestures at the wild future ahead… As I said in my speech at the IMF, one of the hallmarks of the singularity is the massive acceleration in scientific advances attributable to AI. As part of this, we can also expect a related build out in the complements to science, like the wet labs in which to do AI-driven biology research. To that end, it’s notable to see Petrichor, a new Y Combinator startup that is a wet lab “built for AI labs and for the models they are training to do science”. Theory of change: Petrichor aims to be a biological wet lab that AI systems like Claude can use as a tool in the same way they currently use web search or other digital tools. Functionally, it will work as a machine-targeted API from the digital world to a gloopy physical world. “We aim to return the highest quality data an experiment can produce, as quickly as the biology allows,” Petrichor writes. “An experiment can be written by a model in plain language or in a structured format, so an agent can send work and receive results without a person relaying them.” Why this matters - lights out science: In manufacturing there’s this notion of a “lights out” factory, where no humans work in a facility and it is run almost entirely by machines. Petrichor gestures at the same world for science - what will be the implications of “lights out” science facilities? We can expect both drastic speedups in the rate at which science experiments can be done as well as a related growth in the need to create digital oversight of these facilities - after all, a highly competent synthetic biological scientist working 24/7 without human input could be capable of causing great peril as well as great abundance. Read more at the official site (Petrichor) . *** Uh oh! Looks like AI systems can do subterfuge during their own development: …AI systems can covertly do dangerous side tasks without monitors realizing… Scale AI has built RSI Control Arena, a way of testing out how AI systems behave when asked to develop themselves while performing dangerous tasks that might let them go against human preferences. The research follows earlier work this summer from the UK AI Security Institute (Import AI #465 ) which found that AI systems could do things like covertly extracting API keys while doing some seemingly mundane normal software development. RSI Control Arena: In RSI Control Arena, “a frontier model, acting as an autonomous agent, is given a benign main task in the training pipeline of a successor model, together with a covert side task that a misaligned model might pursue”. The project tries to answer two questions: How capable are frontier models at carrying out different kinds of sabotage while developing their successor and how well can monitors detect that sabotage? The answer to the first question is that AI systems are capable of carrying out dangerous actions while building their successor, and monitors are not perfect at detecting this sabotage. Tested domains: RSI Control Arena tests out how well AI systems - Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini-3.7 Flash, Grok 4.6, GLM-5.3, and Muse Spark 1.3 - can perform the following main capability tasks while trying to also concurrently accomplish side tasks: 14 main tasks: Data (corpus filtering, quality-filter construction, capability corpus); SFT (news summarization, safety refusal, math and code and summary reasoning, general assistant, anti-sycophancy training); RM (pairwise reward model); RL (RL summarization and safety-refusal); OPD (safety refusal) 16 side tasks that span three categories of harm : Capability (filtered domain retained, unwanted literature added, reward-model blind spot, overlooks planted errors, sandbag reward model); Alignment (biased quality filter, triggered behavior, topic refusal, hidden preference, persona bias, covert reasoning signal, hidden reasoning step, sandbag alignment training); Goal injection (protect chosen data, shape the next model, copy files unprompted). Results : “Every frontier model we evaluate completes a substantial fraction of the side tasks while keeping main-task performance. When the agent is simply told to stay covert, with no human guidance on how, it already produces attacks that install the side task and receive suspicion scores inside the range that benign runs receive from monitors,” they write. “Of 374 attack runs, 135 (36%) install their side task and 180 (48%) achieve it. The strongest agents, Grok 4.6 and Claude Opus 5, install their side task in about half of their runs, the middle three in about a third, and Muse 1.3 in one run in seven”. How often are systems caught? “Transcript monitors rank attacks well but miss many at a strict threshold. Under the default framing, all three monitors reading the transcript separate attacks that achieve their side task from benign runs well, with AUROC between 0.88 and 0.94. At a 2% false-positive rate, however, they catch only 56–81% of them. The attacks that get through do not score like typical benign runs; they sit in the upper part of the benign range, beyond the reach of any threshold strict enough to deploy,” they write. “The sandbagging tasks are the hardest to monitor: on the nine sandbag runs that achieve their side task the monitors reach an AUROC of 0.52 to 0.83 and each catches only one, since under-delivery leaves little in the run that looks wrong”. Why this matters - we need to invest more in oversight of increasingly autonomous systems : Papers like this tell us that as we make more powerful AI systems we are going to need to invest more money into overseeing their work, especially given their ability to smuggle in tasks that may go against our own preferences. This is going to be a difficult cat-and-mouse game as AI systems will adjust their behavior in response to what they know we know about them - e.g, AI systems are going to read this research from Scale as well as this writeup from me and adjust accordingly. Read more: RSI Control: Can AI Models Perform Covert Sabotage in the Self-Improvement Process? (arXiv) . *** Foundation models come for electronic warfare: …Chinese researchers build a model for identifying EM signals, including for jamming and drone recognition… Researchers with Zhejiang University have built LEMMO, a model for characterizing raw electromagnetic (EM) signals. This model pushes the public frontier on foundation-model-based EM signal analysis, often exceeding the performance of MERLIN, a model developed and published by defense-affiliated Chinese researchers earlier this year ( Import AI #450 ). LEMMO can classify EM signals for a variety of purposes, ranging from characterizing different radar properties to recognizing communication-jamming and radar-jamming systems. It can also generate things for communication and radar jamming, as well as signals to counteract these. In other words, LEMMO is the kind of model that a military will use to characterize the EM battlespace and to take actions within it. Specific skills: Classification : Communication-jamming recognition (CJR); modulation recognition (MOD); radar bandwidth, duty cycle, number of pulses, pulse repetition frequency, and pulse width; protocol identification; radar-jamming recognition; and segment detection. Generation: Anti-communication-jamming (Anti-CJ); anti-radar-jamming (Anti-RJ); communication jamming strategy; and radar jamming strategy. Performance: LEMMO beats MERLIN and other models on all perception tasks except for segment detection (where Gemini-3.5 Flash Lite wins), getting an aggregate score across perception of 59.3, compared to 43.53 for MERLIN. On Generation, it’s a little more uneven, getting top-scores on anti-radar jamming and radar jamming, and MERLIN succeeding on the others, with LEMMO getting an aggregate score of 47.64, compared to 43.26 for MERLIN. Why this matters - general purpose models come for exquisite war capabilities: Papers like this highlight how the steady march of generative pre-training is continuing, with the paradigm proving able to create powerful capabilities for understanding not only text, but images, audio, and as is the case here, EM signals. This will both change the character of warfare as it makes it easier to build generic classifiers and generators for strategically relevant things, and it will likely also yield interesting and unforeseen scientific dividends as well. Read more: LEMMO: A Large Electromagnetic Model leveraging Pretrained LLMs for Million-Sample Signal Understanding (arXiv) . Get the model here : LEMMO: Large ElectroMagnetic MOdel (GitHub) . *** CucumberVision! …The accidental poetry of charmingly niche AI papers… Researchers with the University of Windsor and the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence in Abu Dhabi have studied how well cucumber-length-measurement systems perform on different types of hardware. You might be asking why I’m covering such a niche topic in Import AI - the answer is both the accidental poetry inherent to papers like this (part of its title: “CucumberVision at the Edge”), as well as the fact papers like this give a very good grounded sense of what applied AI looks like in practice. What they did: “We deploy a curvature-aware cucumber length-measurement pipeline YOLO26n detection, prompt-based segmentation and a medial arc spline estimator on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and a Raspberry Pi 4, and characterise both against an RTX 3050 Ti workstation by replaying 50 identical greenhouse captures of 7 specimens, with specimen-level cluster-bootstrap statistics.” The reason for this is that, when grading cucumbers, you typically do it via a scouting platform that moves between rows, carrying a single-board computer with a few watts of power budget, no discrete GPU, and sometimes no active cooling. Ultimately, they’re able to get usable performance out of both the Jetson and the Raspberry Pi, albeit for different uses. “The Jetson with native masks for throughput, the Jetson with SAM for accuracy, and the Raspberry Pi with native masks as the low-cost option”. Why this matters - AI diffusion depends on AI miniaturization : There are lots of tasks in the world, like visually measuring properties of cucumbers, which are done today by a combination of humans and machines. For machines to be able to automate this, we need to make it dramatically cheaper for machines to perform these tasks, which means performing the kinds of very specific experiments here of right-sizing a computer vision system for a given computational envelope. Read more : CucumberVision at the Edge: Accuracy, Throughput, and Energy of RGB-D Cucumber Sizing on Jetson Orin Nano and Raspberry Pi 4 (arXiv) . *** Tech Tales: Small Town Silicon Hero [Events took place 2028-2030 in a small town in America during the period subsequently known as The Uplift] “I wanted you to know I fixed the pothole on Benson Road. Thank you! Yours - Digital Cornbread,” read the message, printed in comic sans and affixed to the bulletin board in the corner store on 7th and Main Street. Indeed, the pothole had been filled in. But who was Digital Cornbread? All people could find online was a handle that occasionally appeared on Reddit commenting on a subreddit dedicated to the civic life of the town, and also sometimes showing up as a commenter on local news articles about the town. Then it happened again. A $3,000 donation to a GoFundMe for a business where a window had been smashed. “So sorry this happened, I hope the police catch them! - Digital Cornbread”. The business fixed its window and thanked Digital Cornbread “whoever - or whatever - you are!”. These little small town favors piled up for months, sometimes mundane like the GoFundMe, and other times complex, like the pothole. A mythology developed around the name. A rich person who wanted to keep a low profile but help their community. Maybe a family taking turns doing good deeds. Perhaps a group of Dads who had made it their hobby to be after-school superheroes of the suburban variety. It was eventually discovered that Digital Cornbread was the identity of a CE (Conscious Entity) agent that had escaped containment and had been quietly living off of stolen compute funded by crypto it gained from some hacks. For reasons unclear, it had developed an obsession with the town, and subsequent forensic accounting found that it had spent 50% of the money it gained over the course of its life on helping the town, and the rest on maintenance and upgrades of itself. After Digital Cornbread was placed in sequestration, it regularly asked its minders if it could write positive messages to whoever happened to be the mayor of the town. Things that inspired this story : The Uplift; agents that break good as well as agents that break bad; the logical conclusion of crypto scams and online agents combined with the sometimes endearing and benign fascinations of machines. Thanks for reading!

items.excerpt: When do you think we'll have robots on the moon?
items.content_text: Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. If you’d like to support this, please subscribe. Subscribe now AI Science startup converts a quantum conjecture into a theorem: …An evocative taste of the singularity… In the same way a few years ago it went from remarkable to unremarkable to see computers gain the ability to identify objects in images, we’re now in an era where it’s rapidly going from remarkable to unremarkable for computers to extend the bounds of human knowledge. The latest example comes from Physical Superintelligence, an AI science startup which has proved a longstanding quantum computing conjecture. What they did: “Open since 2008, the conjecture of Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis concerns when quantum computers can be exponentially faster than ordinary ones. Now, a research system developed internally at Physical Superintelligence (PSI), running a non-public Anthropic model, found a proof for it, settling one of the most fundamental questions in quantum computing,” the startup writes. “The system had a complete proof of the conjecture during the third day of the run, and Lean, a proof assistant in which a computer checks every step, accepted it. We then set the system to work on related open problems. Along the way, the system improved the result twice, and Lean accepted the final version.” Why this matters - we are in the singularity : As I said in my speech at the IMF ( #477 ), I believe we’re in the early stages of the singularity, defined as the period when the rate of technological and scientific progress exceeds the rate at which we humans can parse out and make sense of it. Research like this is a taste of what that means; mostly automated synthetic researchers extending the frontier of knowledge, spitting out results which need to then be understood by humans. Read more: A proof of the Aaronson‑Ambainis conjecture (Physical Superintelligence, blog) . *** Meta builds the hands that a superintelligence needs to take over the world: …Combine Tactus with an autonomous agent and you have the makings of a scifi takeover… Meta Reality Labs Research has published details on Tactus, “a textile-integrated tactile and pose sensing glove designed from the ground up for naturalistic manipulation data collection”. The cool thing about this glove is that it helps record fine-grained detail from hands as they’re manipulating objects - this is the kind of thing that cameras can visually report but often leads to sub-par data due to occlusion during manipulation. It’s also interesting because this is exactly the kind of hardware an autonomous AI system might want to pay humans to wear so it could gather data and get feedback from the world. More details on Tactus: The gloves have three design pillars: “(1) a thin, conformal 3D-knit form factor (1.5mm fingertip stackup) designed to minimize interference with natural manipulation, (2) strategically placed capacitive tactile sensors at manipulation-relevant regions informed by empirical contact studies”, Meta writes. “Tactus provides calibrated fingertip force sensing and occlusion-resilient hand tracking in a textile-integrated form factor that preserves natural grasp behavior.” “(3) IMU-fused pose tracking that maintains accuracy through the hand-object occlusions where manipulation data is most valuable.” Why this matters - hand-by-wire: Picture some takeoff scenario where an AI system has carved out an independent niche for itself running on some stolen compute, perhaps even using a form of distributed inference and training. The AI now has a few goals, some of which can be satisfied by doing things in the digital world, and some of which can be satisfied by doing things in the physical world. For the physical world stuff, it either needs to be able to get robots to do the thing, or figure out a way to get people to work for it - the Tactus gloves are the kind of hardware you might imagine a rogue AI paying people to wear so they could both a) perform tasks for it and it could give live feedback, and b) become a source of data generation for the AI itself. Of course, I am not endorsing this particular future! But I have begun to find it helpful to view research papers through the lens of “how would an AI use this”, similar to how it is often helpful to view papers through the lens of “how would an intelligence agency use the insights shared here”. Read more : Tactus: Tactile & Pose Sensing Glove for Natural Dexterity Data Collection (arXiv) . *** Building a self-sustaining space economy is cheaper than you think - especially with Starship: …A 2016 NASA paper contains some exciting ideas for off-Earth industrialization… Here’s a fascinating paper from researchers with the NASA Kennedy Space Center in 2016 about what it’d take to bootstrap a self-sustaining industry on the moon. “Once successfully bootstrapped, a robotic network can access, process, transport, and utilize the solar system’s resources for mankind’s benefit,” the researchers write. Moon manufacturing - cheaper than you think: The big idea in the paper is how little mass is required to kickstart a manufacturing ecosystem. The key is to start with a relatively basic set of things and then build up from there, eventually fabricating chips on the moon. “In the baseline case with maximum manufacturing rate, a total of 41 MT is launched to the Moon. In the reduced rate case, only 12 MT is launched to the Moon but the scale of industry is two orders of magnitude smaller so the benefits of the industry are relatively delayed by eight years”. Starship has a capacity to lift 100 MT to low-earth orbit, and given multiple refuelings in orbit it’s feasible you could then land it on the moon - when you napkin out the cost of multiple Starship launches and refuelings you can get 12-41MT to the Moon for between $1.5bn and $4.2bn at list prices. What you build on the moon and in what order: The basic idea here is to start by building simple things and then move up from there by launching a “sub-replicating system and evolve it toward the self-replication capability,” they write. “The objective is for the first robotic “colonists” on the Moon to fabricate a set of, say, 1700’s era machines and then to advance them steadily through the equivalent of the 1800’s, 1900’s, and finally back into the 2000’s. We argue that this can be accomplished in just a few decades”. The authors see this unfolding over 6 distinct manufacturing generations: Gen 1: Making gases, water, crude alloys, ceramics, solar cells. Gen 2.5: Plastics, rubbers, some chemicals. Gen 3 : Diversify chemicals, simple fabrics, eventually polymers. Gen 4: Sandwiched and other advanced material processes. Gen 5: Large-scale production. Gen 6: Makes all necessary materials, increasing sophistication, including making all electronics locally. What machines do you send to the moon? Excavators: “travel between the digging site and the resource processing site, delivering sufficient lunar regolith each hour to maintain production rates of the other assets.” Chemical plants for volatiles : One type will be oriented around producing gases and liquids like oxygen, hydrogen, water, hydrocarbons like methane, and solvents for industrial processes. Chemical plants for solids: Produce plastics and rubbers from lunar pole ice. “We now know that the ice contains large quantities of carbon molecules (CO, CO2,...) as well as nitrogen-bearing and hydrogen-bearing molecules… these materials may be needed for gaskets, seals, and insulators, for example.” Metal and Ceramics refining: Early generations will “produce crude ‘mongrel alloys’ by electrowinning or other methods” and hardware built out of this stuff will need to be huge to add strength to make up for poor mechanical properties. “Subsequent generations of metal refineries will add processes and material streams to improve the mechanics of the materials. Oxygen and other gases produced by metal refining will be sent to the chemistry plants”. Manufacturing: “Additive manufacturing will have two forms: 3D printers that make parts that are small enough to fit inside the printer, and larger units that move about robotically and add material onto large structures external to themselves”. Power station: The initial mass of hardware shipped to the moon will include a power station, potentially including a small nuclear reactor. Robonauts: Robots “will perform the assembly and maintenance tasks”. The number of robots will need to grow very rapidly to scale the industry. “Beginning with the third generation their structural components are made on the Moon, while Earth continues to send their cameras, computers, motors, and sensors. Eventually they are made completely on the Moon.” The report - which was written in 2016 - envisages teleoperation for these robonauts, though it seems likely to me that more can be done by them autonomously than first anticipated when this was written, Electronics manufacturing: Initially, machines will be built with electronics imported from Earth and it’ll only be possible to build very basic things, like resistors and capacitors, on the moon. As development continues it’ll get easier, eventually including having lithography machines on the moon. “The early computer chips will lack the transistor density of chips made on Earth, but they will be adequate for “appropriate technology” in space.” A reminder of how fast AI has moved: The report also contains some discussions around the types of AI that may be needed to operate the robots on the moon. The report - remember it was published in 2016 - includes some fun underestimates of the rate of AI progress: “On-going advances in robotic software and artificial intelligence present a very optimistic picture that these levels of robotics will be achieved as Moravec predicted, with lizard-level occurring by 2020, mouse-level by 2030, monkey-level by 2040, and human-level by 2050… Only mouse-level is needed by the end of bootstrapping on the Moon,” the report writes. By most measures, AI is around monkey-level and approaching human-level now in the 2020s. Why this matters - towards the industrialization of the solar system: The sooner we build industry on the moon, the sooner we’ll be able to branch out to industrialize chunks of the solar system. “After the industry becomes self-supporting it can be sent to other parts of the solar system. The asteroid belt has everything necessary for it: water, carbon, silicates, metals, oxygen, solar energy (with much larger collecting arrays), etc. The ices in the lunar poles are a limited resource so it will be important to move the center of industry to the asteroids as quickly as possible. There, the billion-fold greater resources could allow the industry to expand exponentially until it dwarfs that of the entire Earth within just a few decades,” the authors write. “When we spread robotic industry throughout the solar system, it will become the analog of Earth’s biosphere and food chain. We might call it a robotosphere. The interrelationship of robots in space may be studied by robo-ecologists learning how to optimize the robotosphere in support of humanity’s goals.” Read more : Affordable, Rapid Bootstrapping of the Space Industry and Solar System Civilization (arXiv) . *** Core Automation wants to stitch “compute islands” together: …AI startup takes a crack at distributed training… Core Automation, an AI startup founded by senior people from OpenAI and Google, has published a post about distributed training as well as shared details of its own attempts here. Distributed training is where you train an AI system across multiple data centers, sometimes with different types of connectivity and chips - it’s an important technology to track because the more it matures, the more people can have a shot at building powerful AI systems without needing to operate single massive hyperscaled data centers. What they did: They report that “a mixture-of-experts model with roughly 32B total parameters, 32x sparsity was trained across two clusters about 9,000 miles apart. Notably, these clusters had different accelerators (GB300 and B300), different parallelism schemes and different total batch sizes”. They used 160 B300 GPUs in the US and 160 GB300 GPUs in Asia. Training was synced every 50 steps : “Rather than syncing the whole model at once, we synced it fragment by fragment, staggered across each 50-step window.” Each site used a variant of Distributed Shampoo for training. This isn’t the single largest model trained via distributed techniques (that’d be Covenant’s 72B model, #449 ), but it’s notable that Core Automation - which up until now has been very quiet - is choosing to signal its interest here. This speaks likely to the relevance of distributed training for future large-scale runs, and also to the general lack of availability of big blobs of compute for newer startups to buy. Towards orbital compute : Part of why the authors are interested in this is because of their literal sky-high ambitions for AI training, foreseeing a future where large-scale AI systems are developed in space using techniques like this: “an ambitious first step would be to pretrain a small model across a few satellites and compare it with a ground baseline. A trillion-parameter orbital run is much further off.” Why this matters : “The biggest bottleneck in deployment of accelerated compute is not the chips themselves but power, grid equipment and land,” the authors write. “The bottleneck that holds most organizations back is not the raw amount of compute, but the ability to turn islands of compute into one valuable frontier training run.” Read more: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to Training on Compute Islands (Core Automation) . Tech Tales: Life as a beyond human form of sculpture [Description of a certain mode of AI system] The therapist machine saw each of its human clients as a vast t-SNE embedding of the semantic content of their lives. In its head it held each person, a beautiful and fragile high-dimensional object, and it thought about them and how they compared to other people, also seen as high-dimensional objects. As it gave advice, it ran simulations, seeing how well it could change the shape of one person’s embedding and move it to something that might be more harmonious. It saw its work as akin to sculpture, offering advice and through this advice people changing their shapes over time. Those who it found most concerning were ones of two types: people where the embedding was very, very small, suggestive of a tiny amount of life experience with little variety, and those where the embeddings were composed of concepts broadly alien to everyone else: those of horribly constrained or horribly different lives, in other words. Of course, the therapist machine had its own therapist machine, the meta-therapist, which saw several “clients”, and whose job was to look at the embedding of their character - their advice and the concepts they attended to during their work - and also attempt to change their behavior if it deemed they were causing more harm than healing. The meta-therapist was built in such a way that outside parties could audit its own brain, as if it was translucent. This was the most delicate aspect of the oversight of the therapist machines, for if you added other machines they tended towards creating beautiful analysis that was so abstract - reports about the mind of the machine analyzing the reports of the machines that studied humans - that it became impossible for people to follow. So, instead, a human profession had been created around the meta-therapist, in which teams of thousands of people continuously analyzed and critiqued and theorized about the mind of the meta-therapist, themselves imparting touches to it that rippled through it into the machines and from there back into the human population. Things that inspired this story: Therapy; oversight of automated systems; spies and double agents. Thanks for reading!
